A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same survey despite substantial restructuring and the subtitle change from Primer to Survey. All pages, figures, equations and references are readable. V2's Appendix A contains an expanded version of v1's main-text Table 1.

before.justification: Although primarily a survey, v1 reports computed sentence-pair examples in Figures 2–4, including ColBERTv2 similarity 0.965 and interaction attributions with similarity 0.618 and error 0.001. Its limitations describe selecting these examples for the paper; they constitute small illustrative empirical analyses.

after.justification: V2 retains the numerical model-output examples in Figures 2–4 and presents a revised interaction-attribution matrix in Figure 4. These illustrative computations qualify as empirical results, although the broader experimental findings discussed throughout the survey are attributed to prior work.

M1.justification: Neither version introduces a new algorithm or model. Newly covered methods are attributed to existing research. Figure 4's change from IG to IJ corrects the name of Integrated Jacobians, which v1 already describes in Section 5.2.1.

E1.justification: The same sentence pairs remain in the three model-output examples. Newly discussed resources, including sentence-relation datasets and Sentence Smith, expand the literature coverage; the survey does not report evaluating models on these additional datasets.

E2.justification: Neither version reports a controlled comparison against a proposed method. Table 1 categorizes surveyed approaches rather than evaluating baselines, and the retained illustrative examples do not constitute a comparative benchmark.

E3.justification: No revised experimental protocol is stated for the retained examples. V2's evaluation section describes procedures used by cited studies. Removing Figure 4's integration-step count reduces documentation but does not establish a changed computation setting.

E4.justification: Figure 4 revises the token-attribution evidence in the case study explaining similarity between the same two sentences. The S3BERT and ColBERT examples remain unchanged. Newly discussed probing and perturbation tests summarize prior research rather than introduce systematic analyses performed by this survey.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals or significance-testing procedures for its illustrative computations. Figure 4's retained attribution error of 0.001 measures approximation error, not statistical uncertainty.

E6.justification: Figures 2–3 retain their results, including similarities 0.76 and 0.965. Figure 4 retains similarity 0.618 and error 0.001 but changes individual attributions, including the beer/EOS interaction's sign. V2 also adds cited qualitative outcomes, such as anchor features approaching reference-model accuracy; these are not new controlled performance gains.

T1.justification: V2 Section 3.3 corrects the box-containment condition: o(a,b)/s_b equals 1 when b is contained in a, whereas v1 Section 3.2.2 reverses that relationship. Other mathematical descriptions are shortened, including the explicit exact-IJ guarantee. No new theorem or proof is introduced.

C1.justification: V1 presents a three-family primer centered on similarity explanations. V2 broadens the stated contribution to a taxonomy of inherently interpretable embeddings and post-hoc explanations, evaluation synthesis and overarching lessons. Its concluding Perspective additionally argues that most surveyed approaches transfer to decoder-derived embedding models.

C2.justification: V2 substantially expands discussion of explanation evaluation, surrogate-model limitations, context-dependent similarity, RAG explanations and applicability to modern embedding models. Its limitations newly acknowledge outdated evaluated models. Conversely, it removes v1's specific warning about misleading contextualized-token alignments and its caution against comparing methods through isolated examples.

D1.justification: Appendix Table 1 adds code-resource links and replaces Sun et al.'s link, which previously pointed to Benara et al.'s repository. However, v2 removes the per-method inference-cost column and Figure 4's explicit N=50 integration steps. These change available technical documentation without establishing altered underlying methods.

R1.justification: V2 integrates substantial additional literature on anchors, sparsification, global explanations and surrogate/probing methods, including SPLADE and Conneau's probing work. Some references disappear, including Zhang et al. (2020), despite BERTScore remaining discussed. Sun and Fodor publication-year updates represent retained works rather than new additions.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, method descriptions, discussion and limitations undergo extensive rewriting. Three standalone method families become a hierarchy under Interpretable Embeddings and Post-hoc Explanation; evaluation receives a dedicated section, and the former conclusion becomes an expanded Perspective. Title and authorship details also change.

P2.justification: Figure 1 is comprehensively redrawn around the expanded taxonomy. Table 1 is reorganized into hierarchical groups, expanded, moved to Appendix A and stripped of its inference-cost column. Figure 4 is replotted with revised axis labels and caption; Figures 2–3 retain their plotted results with placement or caption edits.

improvement.justification: V2 fills substantial gaps in the survey's coverage through sparse embeddings, global explanations and surrogate/probing methods. Its clearer taxonomy and new Section 5.1 explain how explanation quality is evaluated and why comparisons are difficult, substantially improving its usefulness as a survey. These gains outweigh the loss of specific alignment caveats, Figure 4 computation details and the BERTScore source citation.
